correctness.rationale: Fu–Li Theorem 4.4 reduces MS_B on a polyhedral Radon plane exactly to the largest norm distance between Birkhoff-orthogonal extreme points. The polar of the inradius-one regular N=4m+2 polygon becomes cos(alpha) times the primal polygon after a quarter-turn, so the plane is Radon. At a fixed vertex, the adjacent two norming facets show that, modulo sign, only vertex indices m and m+1 can be Birkhoff-orthogonal. The resulting two Euclidean chords have lengths 2 sec(alpha) sin(pi/4 minus or plus alpha/2), and their directions have parity-dependent distance 0 or alpha from the facet-normal lattice. This gives the two displayed polygonal norms. The plus chord is strictly larger in both parity cases, producing the modulo-8 formula.
risks: The Radon conclusion uses the standard planar polar/antinorm characterization; the concrete quarter-turn polar identity is stated explicitly.
The checker is finite and supplementary; the proof itself classifies all possible orthogonal extreme-point indices for every m.

value.rationale: MS_B was introduced as a quantitative orthogonality constant and Fu–Li singled out Radon planes as the setting where it becomes an exact orthogonal-chord invariant. Regular 4m+2-gons are the canonical polygonal Radon family, so an exact all-m formula is a natural missing benchmark rather than an arbitrary slice. The modulo-8 split is structural: it records whether the longer orthogonal vertex chord lies on a facet-normal or vertex ray, and it yields a nontrivial decagonal golden-ratio value. The result also quantifies convergence of this canonical polygonal Radon family toward the Hilbert endpoint sqrt(2).
risks: The theorem is an exact canonical-family computation, not a classification of MS_B over all Radon planes.
